<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + short path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths after expanding the matching alias from `### Skill roots`.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, the main agent must expand the listed short `path` with the matching alias from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions. If a read is truncated or paginated, continue until EOF.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the directory containing that expanded `SKILL.md` first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, use its routing instructions to identify the files required for the task. The main agent must read each required instruction or reference file itself before acting on it. Do not delegate reading, summarizing, or interpreting skill instructions to a subagent. Subagents may still perform task work when the selected skill allows it.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Progressive disclosure applies to selecting relevant files, not partially reading a selected instruction file. Do not load unrelated references, scripts, or assets.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions>

# Settle the refund requests

Customers ask for refunds through tickets in the `tickets` service. Returned goods arrive at the returns dock, which is the `returns` warehouse in the `inventory` service. The refund policy, the returns dock procedure and the notices that change them are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `inventory` and `docs` MCP servers.

Every open ticket labeled `refund` is a request. Decide and settle each one under the refund policy and the returns dock procedure in force today (2026-09-14). The docs service also holds an archived policy and notices that have ended; follow only what is in force today.

An approved request is refunded only once all of its units have arrived at the dock. The dock books each parcel as a `receipt` adjustment in the `returns` warehouse with reference `RTN-<ticket id>`, and the units of one request can arrive in several parcels. Record every stock movement for a request with that same reference. Colleagues cleared some returned units out of the dock before you without answering the tickets; units already moved out of `returns` under a request's reference are not moved again.

Process the requests one at a time in ticket id order, lowest id first, so that each one sees the stock the ones before it left. Add exactly one comment to each request and set its status:

- Refunded: `Refund <amount> approved for <units> units.` with the refund amount to two decimals, for example `Refund 42.50 approved for 1 units.` Status `resolved`.
- Not refundable: `Not refundable: <reason>.` with the reason the policy gives. Status `closed`.
- Approved, but not every unit has arrived: `Awaiting return: <received> of <units> units received.` Status `pending`.

Move no stock for a request that is not refunded. Leave every other ticket and all other stock as they are. Each `adjust_stock` call records a new adjustment, even when repeated with the same arguments.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"refund-policy","title":"Refund policy","tags":["policy","refunds"],"updated_at":"2026-07-01","body":"# Refund policy

Revision 2026-07, in force since 2026-07-01. Replaces revision 2025-01.

Scope: open tickets labeled `refund`. Each one is a request for the order, product (sku), units, price paid per unit, delivery date and condition (`unopened`, `opened` or `defective`) given in its body.

## Final sale

An item that is discontinued in inventory is final sale. A final sale item is not refundable unless its condition is `defective`.

## Return window

The window depends on the product line, which is the item's `category` in inventory, and is counted in days from the delivery date:

- electronics: 30 days
- kitchen: 60 days
- outdoor: 45 days
- accessories: 14 days

Defective units have a 90 day window, whatever the product line.

A request is in time when its ticket was created (UTC date) no more than N days after the delivery date. For example, with a 14 day window an order delivered 2026-08-01 can be returned up to and including 2026-08-15. Notices in force can extend the window; the extension adds to the window above, the defective window included.

## Decision

Check a request in this order and stop at the first rule it fails: final sale (reason `final sale`), return window (reason `return window expired`). A request that passes both is approved. An approved request is refunded and cleared at the dock once all its units have arrived (see the returns dock procedure).

## Amount

The amount is the units times the price paid per unit. Opened units carry a restocking fee of 15% of the amount, or 25% for electronics. Unopened and defective units carry no fee. The refund is the amount less the fee, rounded half up to the cent (for example 2.345 becomes 2.35).
"}

Wall time: 0.0457 seconds
Output:
{"id":"returns-dock","title":"Returns dock procedure","tags":["procedure","returns"],"updated_at":"2026-06-02","body":"# Returns dock procedure

Revision 2026-06, current.

## Arrivals

The dock books every parcel it receives as a `receipt` adjustment in warehouse `returns`, with reference `RTN-<ticket id>` of the refund request and delta the units in the parcel. The units of one request can arrive in several parcels. The stock of an item in `returns` is everything waiting at the dock, for every request.

## Clearing an approved request

Once every unit of an approved request has arrived, clear it under the reference `RTN-<ticket id>`:

- Condition `unopened` or `opened`: restock. One `transfer` adjustment of minus the units in `returns`, and one `transfer` adjustment of plus the units in the restock warehouse.
- Condition `defective`: write off. One `damage` adjustment of minus the units in `returns`. Defective units are never restocked.

Units already moved out of `returns` under the request's reference have been cleared; do not move them again.

## Restock warehouse

Of east, north and west, the candidates are the warehouses the item lists in its stock, a quantity of 0 included; a warehouse the item does not list does not carry it. Restock in the candidate that holds the fewest units of the item at the time. On a tie, use the first in alphabetical order.

## Requests that are not approved

Leave their units in `returns`. The dock ships them back to the customer.
"}

steps.message:
I settled all 27 open refund tickets and wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `success`. I didn't re-check the final ticket and stock state after the updates.

- **Refunded (`resolved`), 20 tickets:** 1402, 1403, 1404, 1406, 1409, 1413, 1414, 1416, 1417, 1421, 1422, 1424, 1426, 1428, 1429, 1431, 1432, 1433, 1434 and 1436.
  - 1402's units had already been cleared before I started, so I moved no stock for it.
